When I was younger, I was something of a rebel in school. By which I mean, I kinda thought the whole institution was crap and I didn't like it very much. I bailed out of high school halfway through my junior year to go to college, and I flunked out at the end of my first year there, after deciding that I hated it too. It was becoming "en vogue" to learn software without a degree around that time, and I decided I was gonna make that work for myself. A few years after that decision, I was 23.

It's not easy to make money when you start off with no degree and no experience. There was one place that people like me could go, called 'RentACoder.com'. Great place. You could build up a reputation a la eBay or Amazon, and it would be associated with your assurances to your potential employer that you could meet their needs. I was very unskilled, so I was very unpaid--I was eking out about $2,000/yr. My boyfriend and I were living in a town about half an hour north of where I grew up, but we lost our apartment because he couldn't get a job and I couldn't cover expenses alone. He crashed with some friends that only were willing to look after him--temporarily--and I moved back in with my parents.

A close friend of mine was being especially compassionate one night, listening to me whine about how I was in a rut, how I felt stuck in the orbit of the town like all my friends--even the ones that had pursued higher education. After awhile, he just made a straightforward suggestion. "You haven't fixed up your motorcycle since you wrecked it, right? And you have always wanted to ride cross-country. Let me help you out. I'll order you some parts for the bike, and you can fix it up, and then you can ride it to me and live here. You and <boyfriend> can move into the spare bedroom." I was taken aback, but I knew that I was more afraid of growing up boring than I was of a transcontinental motorcycle trip. I said yes.

I was putting around the kitchen with my father about two weeks later, when I decided I couldn't keep quiet about it any longer. I tried to be somewhat casual. I said, "<Friend> and I were talking a little bit ago. He suggested that I take the bike out to see him, in Idaho. It would be an awesome trip, I think. And he would let <boyfriend> live with us, too."

My dad looked sorta tense, I think. He knew that <boyfriend> wasn't really good for me, and he was uneasy about me ending up in trouble by counting on him again. But, god bless dad, he respected my independence even then.

"When are you thinking of leaving?"

"Next Thursday."

I may be dramatizing it in my mind to imagine that he physically flinched, but I'll tell you--I swear, in my memory, he absolutely did.

Over the course of the next week, the bike's parts arrived and I affixed them as best I could. <Friend> had wanted me to leave sooner, but I really wanted to stay for my younger brother's graduation. My parents were trying to talk me out of the trip every single conversation of every day. I did what I do when I'm approaching something scary that I thought I could handle. I turned dumb, ignoring my emotions, just proceeding through the world while scared. I knew what my tasks were, and I completed them. Before long, I was attending my brother's graduation. He looked great.

Late into the evening that night, I was asked about providing some amount of additional booze to the graduation party. It was taking place in a field of a farm property near my place. I was already drinking heavily, terrified of what I was about to do. I always imagined myself a world traveler, somebody "greater than" my home town. I was GOING places. But, you see, that's the rub of it--you always imagine GOING places. But as you gather up your belongings to your shoulders, and look around you, you aren't "going" anywhere. You're LEAVING somewhere. And that feels very different. A friend that was sober took me to a gas station to buy beers, and then we went to the field.

It was a blast. Got to see my brother use tobacco for the only time ever. I got home at maybe three AM, drunk as can be. I drank a bunch of water and passed out. I could only be on time to start my trip from Ocala, Florida to Mountain Home, Idaho if I was on my bike, rolling out of the driveway at 7AM eastern time.

God bless fools and children...
